entities.summary: John Philpot Curran was an Irish orator, politician, and lawyer celebrated for his defence of civil and political liberty. He first won popular acclaim in 1780, as the only lawyer in his circuit willing to represent a Catholic priest horsewhipped by an Anglo-Irish lord. In the 1790s he was celebrated as a champion in the Irish House of Commons of Catholic emancipation and parliamentary reform, and in court as defence counsel for United Irishmen facing charges of sedition and treason. Following the rebellion of 1798, he was vocal in his opposition to Britain's incorporation of Ireland in a United Kingdom.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: John Philpot Curran's advocacy for Catholic emancipation and parliamentary reform in 18th-century Ireland had significant regional impact, influencing Irish politics and contributing to the eventual repeal of the Act of Union in 1801.
